chunks: My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Al-Husayn ibn Yazid al-Nawfaly, from Isma'il ibn Abi Ziyad, from Abu Abdillah, from his forefathers, peace be upon them.

He said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever begins with speech before greeting, do not respond to him.' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not invite anyone to your food until he greets you.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on responding to someone who speaks before greeting you?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq highlights the precedence of the greeting (salam) as a fundamental social protocol, linking verbal initiation to spiritual respect. This narration underscores the etiquette of humility in communal gatherings, where the act of greeting serves as a prerequisite for meaningful engagement and hospitality.
